diagnosis.primary: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4, left frontal lobe.

presentation.presenting_complaint: First-time focal seizure (right arm jerking, no loss of consciousness) after 6 weeks of worsening headaches and word-finding difficulty.
presentation.hpi_summary: Previously healthy 58F brought to the ED after a focal seizure involving the right arm. Six weeks of progressive morning headaches and intermittent word-finding difficulty. ED MRI (study _000) showed a necrotic enhancing left frontal mass with vasogenic edema and rightward midline shift. Started on dexamethasone and levetiracetam; subtotal resection on 2026-05-19 confirmed glioblastoma. Completed standard chemoradiation on 2026-07-24 and started adjuvant temozolomide on 2026-08-24.

active_problems: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, left frontal lobe — status post subtotal resection and chemoradiation, on adjuvant temozolomide.
Structural epilepsy (single focal seizure at presentation), seizure-free on levetiracetam.
Mild expressive aphasia, improving with speech therapy.
past_medical_history: No prior cranial surgery or cranial irradiation.

medications.name: temozolomide
medications.dose: 150 mg/m² PO on days 1–5 of each 28-day cycle

procedures.procedure: Left frontal craniotomy and subtotal tumor resection
procedures.result: Subtotal resection. Residual enhancing tumor left along the posterior-medial cavity wall to protect language and motor pathways.

treatments.treatment: Radiation therapy, 60 Gy in 30 fractions, to the left frontal resection cavity and margin, with concurrent temozolomide 75 mg/m² daily
